features.description: Read-only self-service portal where a tenant's Business Partner opens a magic link and sees their completed invoices, outstanding balance and invoice PDFs. The portal surface, its three /sws/portal/* endpoints and the access table are UNCONDITIONAL; the flag gates only whether the sales-invoice email carries the link, and is targeted at the ETGO_ACCOUNT email of the user sending the invoice.

flag.$symbolsComment: Backend-only flag: no frontend symbol exists because nothing in the browser evaluates it and no key is declared in flag-keys.js. Deliberate -- see $gatingComment. The property and env-var spellings are listed because a grep for the bare key misses Openbravo.properties and the ECS task definition. Per-account enablement leaves NO grep trail in this repo at all: it is a targeting rule in the backend's hosted control plane -- Datadog Feature Flags when DD_FEATURE_FLAGS_ENABLED (dd.feature.flags.enabled) is set and dd-java-agent is loaded, else the ConfigCat dashboard when an SDK key is set (ETP-5751) -- so the registry is the only place that records where to look.

features.$gatingComment: ONE GATE: this flag, evaluated PER SENDING ACCOUNT. Default false -- no link goes out until a targeting rule on the hosted control plane (Datadog Feature Flags, or ConfigCat as the fallback) names an ETGO_ACCOUNT email. That answers 'depende del usuario logueado' (the user's words) with the flag itself rather than a second mechanism. TARGETING IS A PLATFORM CAPABILITY, NOT PORTAL CODE: GoFeatureFlags.createProvider() installs, in order (ETP-5751): the Datadog OpenFeature provider when DD_FEATURE_FLAGS_ENABLED (dd.feature.flags.enabled) is true AND dd-java-agent is loaded (the Datadog environment is DD_ENV); else the ConfigCat provider when etendo.go.configcat.sdkKey (ETGO_CONFIGCAT_SDK_KEY) resolves; else PropertiesFeatureProvider -- so any future backend flag gets per-account targeting free -- the user asked for it on those terms ('nos sirve para otras funcionalidades'). The account email is the targeting key and is also published as the 'email' attribute, LOWERCASED, which is what Datadog rules match on (their ONE_OF/MATCHES comparisons are case-sensitive and every rule value is lowercase), and, for the ConfigCat fallback, as the 'Email' attribute as stored, because ConfigCat's ContextTransformer maps the key to its identifier and only a literal 'Email' attribute to the email. Evaluation is in memory, an undefined flag resolves to the false code default, and a rule change is live with no restart on either hosted arm (ConfigCat within one poll interval). With neither hosted arm configured the flag degrades to a plain per-environment boolean: fine on a dev box (one user), but a shared environment needs Datadog (or ConfigCat) configured before it is switched on for anyone. THE IDENTITY IS THE ETGO_ACCOUNT EMAIL, NOT AD_User.email: onboarding never writes AD_User.email (InitialSetupUtility only writes username, as EtendoGoJwtDalHelper documents), so targeting the AD user's email would read null for essentially every GO user and match nobody -- PortalLinkPolicy resolves the account via GoAccountResolver instead. No account, no email, or a failed lookup means no link, never allow. THREE shapes were tried and rejected on 2026-09-10 before this one: an environment flag ANDed with a per-sender AD_Preference (nothing worked until two unrelated things were configured), the AD_Preference alone with no flag, and an etendo.go.flags.<key>.emails property allowlist in PropertiesFeatureProvider (removed because it is inert wherever an SDK key is set -- a knob that silently does nothing is the ETP-4966 shape again). This does NOT reopen targeting-key-divergence on paid-second-tenant: that divergence needs two evaluators disagreeing, and this flag is backend-only with no frontend key -- none must ever be added. But note a hosted control plane in the backend (Datadog, or ConfigCat) makes a SHARED flag newly possible, so that item must be closed before any flag is read on both ends (ETP-4966).
features.$pathsComment: Owned code = the portal feature itself, which is deleted only if the FEATURE is killed. It is NOT deleted when the flag retires: the flag gates one conditional in the email contract, so shipping it unwraps that conditional and leaves every path here in place (same shape as paid-second-tenant, which kept its paths after tenant-upgrade retired). Shared touch points, NOT owned: the sales-invoice email contract, runtime-routes.jsx, GoFeatureFlags, and PropertiesFeatureProvider -- the per-account targeting added there is a platform capability that outlives this flag and must not be removed with it.

features.description: Automatic bounce-pair suggestions in the bank reconciliation of PSD2-synced financial accounts in Etendo. A bounce is an outgoing bank-statement line plus the line that reverses it (same amount, opposite sign). With the flag on, the backend auto-match detects candidate pairs, the auto-match modal shows them in a 'Rechazos bancarios' section and they can be reviewed in the reconciliation panel; accepting a pair logically discards BOTH statement lines (EM_PSD2_IS_DISCARDED) and links them as a pair, and discard and restore always act on the pair. Honouring lines that are already discarded is gated too (option 2, ETP-5581): with the flag on they are excluded from the pending lists, auto-match and reconciliation (only while unmatched; a reconciled line counts as reconciled) and count as resolved; with it off Etendo behaves as before ETP-5581 and a discarded line is a plain pending line, with two declared exceptions that are not gated: the SQL-stored counters (FIN_Financial_Account.EM_ETGO_Pending_Count and FIN_BankStatement.EM_ETGO_Discarded_Count / EM_ETGO_Status; see deferredItems pending-counter-not-gated) and the statement-edit identity fix (a recreated line keeps its PSD2 transaction id and discard flag, BankStatementLineSet), which changes nothing visible with the flag off.

deferredItems.note: Option 2 (ETP-5581) gates every Java read of discarded lines, but three values are computed in SQL or in persistence events, which cannot see a per-account, per-request flag, and keep leaving discarded lines out whatever the flag says: FIN_Financial_Account.EM_ETGO_Pending_Count (stored computed column, function ETGO_ACCOUNT_PENDING_COUNT, watched column EM_PSD2_Is_Discarded) and FIN_BankStatement.EM_ETGO_Discarded_Count / EM_ETGO_Status. The statements list re-derives its status with the flag off, so only the account counter is visible. AND THEREFORE: turning the flag off for an account that already discarded pairs shows its Por conciliar column, its filter, the Conciliacion tab badge and the sidebar count LOWER than the reconciliation panel (e.g. 47 against 49) until the flag is turned back on or the lines are restored in Classic -- approved by the user as a known limitation for the flag's lifetime, no data-fix. On a KILL the change to ETGO_ACCOUNT_PENDING_COUNT must be reverted (count every unmatched line again, drop the EM_PSD2_Is_Discarded watched column) and the counter rebuilt with ad_scd_rebuild; that restores the old counter without a data-fix. On SHIP (feature for everyone) the limitation disappears, because the flag can no longer be off. Not marked acceptedDebt: that needs an explicit decision recorded here by the team.
